so they are active. As in the absolute comparison, first substitute
$\varpi^{dp^i}$ for each occurrence of $\pi_i(\pi)$ in the
product expansion, without reducing the integral coefficients.
Telescope a difference of products by replacing one parameter
occurrence at a time. If the marked occurrence has level
$1\leq i<N$ and monomial degree $\ell$, its error has
$\pi$-valuation $e_n+p^{i-1}$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:uniform-parameter-error}. Its excess over the degree
weight is at least
\[
 e_n+p^{i-1}-\frac\ell\delta
 \geq e_n-\left(\frac{\deg f_i}{\delta}-p^{i-1}\right)
 \geq e_n-\Theta_N.
\]
All other occurrences have nonnegative excess, whether or not they
have already been substituted. Consequently, after including the
basis factor, a product error in row $u$ has valuation at least
\[
 \frac d\delta(pu-v)+d(e_n-\Theta_N)+p^m(v-u)
       =cu+d(e_n-\Theta_N).
\]
There is no parameter error at level zero.

It remains to reduce the coefficients of this intermediate model.
Their reduction errors are divisible by $p$, and
\eqref{eq:uniform-monomial-weight} gives total valuation at least
$cu+de_n$. After division by the row factor this is precision
$de_n\geq d(e_n-\Theta_N)$. Thus the normalized matrices agree to precision
$d(e_n-\Theta_N)$ in both comparisons. In particular, division by the row factor
has not used unavailable precision: both the parameter error and
the coefficient-reduction error were first shown to contain that
row factor together with the additional required power of $\varpi$.

The use of a common quotient is legitimate: $\Theta_N\geq0$
gives $d(e_n-\Theta_N)\leq de_n=L_n$, and $e_n>\Theta_N$ gives $d(e_n-\Theta_N)>0$.
Furthermore $d\Theta_N$ is an integer, because each possible
nonzero value becomes $p^m\deg f_i-dp^{i-1}$ after multiplication
by $d$. Hence $d(e_n-\Theta_N)$ is an integer, and the quotient of length
$d(e_n-\Theta_N)$ is obtained from \eqref{eq:classical-common-quotient} by
further truncation. In particular, coefficient carries vanish
at all precisions used here. The convergent sums and the isometric
coefficient twist preserve the estimates, as in the preceding
proposition.
<!-- end proof-94 -->
<!-- proof-95: body_md -->
For $d\leq2$, every integer is a common contact, so the whole
polygon is fixed for every $n>m$. The characteristic-block
description in Proposition~\ref{prop:KZ-equivalence} gives slope
stability from level $m+1$. Suppose henceforth that $d\geq3$.

The normalized nontrivial contact blocks have rank $d-1$ and
row spacing $c=(p-1)p^m$. Their relative precision threshold is
\[
 \frac{(p-1)p^m}{2}\left\lfloor\frac{(d-1)^2}{4}\right\rfloor
       =p^mC_{\mathrm u}.
\]
We compare the full tower with its finite head, the finite head
with its reduced model, and that model with the reduced full tower.
For the first and third comparisons, apply
Proposition~\ref{prop:uniform-relative-dwork}(i) with $C_0=C_{\mathrm u}$.
The precision is exactly at least the displayed threshold.
Corollary~\ref{cor:relative-contact-comparison} therefore gives
\[
 N_n(f)=N_n(f^{<N})\quad(n\geq N),\qquad
 N_\infty(f^{<N})=N_\infty(f)
\]
on the entire half-line. The finite head has the same contact
indices because $N>m$. The non-strict threshold in the semilinear
precision theorem is used at this step.

Only the middle comparison requires a sufficiently large conductor.
By Proposition~\ref{prop:uniform-relative-dwork}(ii) and the same
block comparison, it suffices that
\[
 d(e_n-\Theta_N)\geq
       \frac{(p-1)p^m}{2}\left\lfloor\frac{(d-1)^2}{4}\right\rfloor.
\]
Dividing by $d$ and using $p^m/d=1/\delta$ gives the more precise
starting condition
\begin{equation}\label{eq:uniform-refined-start}
 n\geq N,\qquad
 (p-1)p^{n-1}\geq\Theta_N+
       \frac{p-1}{2\delta}\left\lfloor\frac{(d-1)^2}{4}\right\rfloor.
\end{equation}
Its last summand is positive for $d\geq3$, so it also ensures
$e_n>\Theta_N$, as required in that proposition. We obtain
$N_n(f^{<N})=N_\infty(f^{<N})$. Combining the three comparisons,
\[
 N_n(f)=N_n(f^{<N})=N_\infty(f^{<N})=N_\infty(f)
\]
on the whole half-line.

To obtain the stated starting level, suppose first that $N\geq2$.
Replace $\Theta_N$ by its upper bound $(p-1)p^{N-2}$ in
\eqref{eq:uniform-refined-start}, and divide by $p-1$. This gives
exactly \eqref{eq:uniform-start}. If $N=1$, then $N>m\geq0$
forces $m=0$, so $\delta=d$ and $\Theta_N=0$. The resulting
inequality is \eqref{eq:uniform-polynomial-start}. Once either
condition holds at $n_0$, it holds at every $n\geq n_0$, since its
right side is fixed and its left side increases. All quantities
in these inequalities depend on the degrees and conductor levels,
not on $a$.

Finally, we spell out how stationarity gives the full stability
rule. By Proposition~\ref{prop:KZ-equivalence}, the first $D_{n_0}$
characteristic slopes are
$a(p-1)p^{n_0-1}(\{0\}\sqcup S_{n_0})$, and successive blocks
are obtained by adding $a(p-1)p^{n_0-1}$. At level $n\geq n_0$,
the first $D_n=p^{n-n_0}D_{n_0}$ slopes of this same polygon consist
of $p^{n-n_0}$ such blocks. Dividing them by $a(p-1)p^{n-1}$ yields
\[
 \{0\}\sqcup S_n
 =\bigsqcup_{j=0}^{p^{n-n_0}-1}
       \frac{j+(\{0\}\sqcup S_{n_0})}{p^{n-n_0}},
\]
as multisets. The zero in the block $j=0$ is the single initial
characteristic zero. The zeros in the other blocks give the grid
$\{j/p^{n-n_0}:1\leq j<p^{n-n_0}\}$, each once. Removing the
initial zero therefore gives exactly the primitive arithmetic-progressions
and grid slopes in the definition of slope stability, with starting
level $n_0$.
<!-- end proof-95 -->
<!-- corollary-27: body_md -->
\label{cor:uniform-head-stability}
Let $n\geq2$ and $n>m$. If
\begin{equation}\label{eq:uniform-finite-head-start}
 (p-1)p^{n-2}\geq
       \frac1{2\delta}\left\lfloor\frac{(d-1)^2}{4}\right\rfloor,
\end{equation}
then the polygon of $f^{<n}$ at every conductor $p^r$, $r\geq n$,
equals $N_n(f)$. The assertion holds for every prime $p$ and every
constant-field degree $a$. For $d\leq2$ no displayed inequality
is needed.
<!-- end corollary-27 -->
<!-- proof-96: body_md -->
Since $n>m$, the finite head has the same ramification parameters
as $f$. Its levels $i\geq n$ vanish, so its tail satisfies every
degree-gap requirement, with $\deg0=-\infty$. For $d\geq3$, apply
Theorem~\ref{thm:uniform-gap} to this head with $N=n$ and proposed
starting level $n_0=n$. Its sufficient condition is
\[
 p^{n-1}\geq p^{n-2}
       +\frac1{2\delta}\left\lfloor\frac{(d-1)^2}{4}\right\rfloor.
\]
Subtracting $p^{n-2}$ gives \eqref{eq:uniform-finite-head-start}.
Thus the head has the same polygon at every level $r\geq n$,
including level $n$ itself. At that level a character of order
$p^n$ kills all Witt terms divisible by $p^n$, so $f$ and $f^{<n}$
have exactly the same character sums and characteristic series.
The common polygon is therefore $N_n(f)$. For $d\leq2$ the
unconditional contact case of the theorem gives the same conclusion.
<!-- end proof-96 -->
<!-- remark-16: body_md -->
Lemma~\ref{lem:head-stability} gives the original finite-head proof
by coefficient estimates. Corollary~\ref{cor:uniform-head-stability}
gives another proof with a starting condition independent of $a$
and with no restriction $p>2$.

It also extends the finite initial-polygon criterion of
Theorem~\ref{thm:all-slope-propagation} to $p=2$. To see precisely
which input changes, retain its hypothesis
\eqref{eq:full-propagation-criterion} and its finite range $1\leq j<A$ in
\eqref{eq:criterion-finite-range}. Choose $n\geq2$, $n>m$, large
enough that $D_n-A_{\mathrm u}>0$,
$D_n-A_{\mathrm u}+1\geq A$, and
\eqref{eq:uniform-finite-head-start} holds. Theorem~\ref{thm:uniform-partial}
then identifies $N_n$ with $N_\infty$ through $A$, while the original
chord bound makes the criterion automatic for $j\geq A$.
The reflection identity \eqref{eq:reflected-excess} consequently
gives
\[
 N_n(k)\leq h(k)+\frac{(p-1)(D_n-k+1)}{\delta}
             \qquad(1\leq k\leq D_n).
\]
The strict tail estimate \eqref{eq:strict-tail-estimate}, valid for
every prime, places all coefficient differences strictly above
this polygon. The new corollary makes the finite-head polygon
equal to $N_n$ at every higher conductor. Its vertices through
$D_n$ are therefore preserved for the full tower, and the common
contact at $D_n+1$ extends the agreement. This is the same conclusion
as \eqref{eq:all-slope-propagation}. The polygon hypothesis remains
necessary for this argument; the new input removes only the
restriction on $p$ in the finite-head step. The finite-check loss $A$
and the vertical polygon gap still depend on $a$, so this application
is not a claim of an
$a$-independent starting level for that separate polygon criterion.
Corollaries~\ref{cor:uniform-small-degree} and
\ref{cor:uniform-eleven} give the direct uniform applications in
small degree and degree eleven.
<!-- end remark-16 -->
<!-- remark-17: body_md -->
The contact-block rank $d-1$ controls the precision in this argument.
The order $a$ of coefficient Frobenius enters only when the one-step
slopes are multiplied by $a$; it does not enter the comparisons
of matrices. This proves the uniform constants and starting levels
in Theorem~\ref{thm:intro-uniform}.

The ordinates of the $q$-Frobenius polygon still scale by $a$, as
does the vertical chord gap in \eqref{eq:general-chord-gap}.
Moreover, the common quotient \eqref{eq:classical-common-quotient}
and the valuations in Lemma~\ref{lem:uniform-parameter-error} use
a classical character of specified conductor. They do not by
themselves compare all points in a weight annulus. The arbitrary-weight
estimates and analytic arguments of Part~\ref{part:positive}
therefore retain their separate role and their stated constants.
<!-- end remark-17 -->
